preview_en:
On the back of their first Bundesliga win of the season in the last round, Hoffenheim look to follow it up against a promoted Paderborn side who are already struggling in the top tier.

Match News and Current Form

Paderborn’s return to the Bundesliga for the first time since 2019/20 hasn’t quite gone according to plan so far as they’re winless and goalless after three rounds (D1, L2). They’ll be quick to point out that their two defeats came against the only two sides with a 100% Bundesliga record after three rounds in Freiburg and Dortmund, but struggling at this level has been a long-standing issue. Paderborn are now winless in their last 18 top-flight games (D6, L12), which is not only the longest current run in the league, but also an unwanted club record, and a rotten home record has greatly contributed to that having lost eight of the last nine Bundesliga fixtures they hosted (D1).

Hoffenheim collected their first Bundesliga win of the campaign when they beat Stuttgart 2-1 last weekend, but they were dealt a harsh reality check in midweek when they lost 2-0 away to OFI Crete in the UEFA Europa League. That’s now three defeats from four competitive games this term for Christian Ilzer’s men, who are at risk of losing three of their opening four Bundesliga matches for only the second time in the last ten years. Winning just two of their last eight top-flight away games (D2, L4) is likely to have them fearing adding to that tally, but some respite could come in the form of opposition here as Hoffenheim have won seven of their last nine Bundesliga road trips against newly-promoted opposition (D1, L1).

Head-to-Head History

Paderborn have never beaten Hoffenheim before (D2, L4), and no team in German professional football has a lower goals-per-game ratio against a single opponent they’ve played at least six times than Paderborn have against Hoffenheim (0.17).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Eleven of Paderborn’s last 12 Bundesliga home games saw both teams score.

Paderborn conceded 3+ goals in five of their last six Sunday-held top-flight home matches.

Hoffenheim have conceded all seven of their Bundesliga goals this season after half-time.

Seven of Hoffenheim’s last nine Bundesliga matches saw the home team on the day score 2+ goals.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Stefano Marino could be the man to get Paderborn off the mark for the campaign, but they may have to be patient if so as six of his eight goals for the club arrived after half-time. Hoffenheim’s Adam Daghim has contributed to a goal in their opening three Bundesliga games (G1, A2) - no player in the club’s history has ever done so in the first four matches of a top-flight season.

Paderborn hope to have Laurin Curda available despite picking up a knock last weekend. Hoffenheim look to be at full strength.

Betting Analysis

Given how difficult Paderborn have found it to adapt, and their home struggles, combining a Hoffenheim win and over 2.5 goals could bear fruit.

Author: Chris Wilson
